evidence.quote: Brex APIs use the REST architecture, are defined using the OpenAPI specification
This guide assumes you are a Brex customer with admin access to your dashboard.
Please contact our developer support team to be issued a client ID and client secret for partner authentication.
54 endpoints (apis.guru OpenAPI spec index for brex.io)
MCP clients that support OAuth will automatically initiate a browser-based authorization flow when you first connect.

result.notes: Two distinct credential paths. (1) Existing Brex customers: an account/card admin logs into dashboard.brex.com, accepts a developer API agreement, and self-issues a bearer token (90-day expiry, scoped) from Settings > Developer — no sandbox, no free signup for non-customers. (2) Third-party/partner integrations: OAuth2 (authorization_code and client_credentials grants) requires contacting Brex developer support to be issued a client ID/secret as a registered partner — this is the path relevant to building a general-purpose agent toolkit and is gated. Brex also publishes an official hosted MCP server (api.brex.com/mcp) supporting both OAuth (per-user, browser flow, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration) and bearer-token auth for non-OAuth MCP clients. API is REST/OpenAPI-based (~54 endpoints per apis.guru spec) covering cards, expenses, transactions, users, budgets, etc.
result.one_liner: Brex is a corporate card and spend-management platform offering a REST API (cards, expenses, transactions, budgets, users) plus an official MCP server for agent access.
